item.title: 🟠 CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
item.description:
Why this matters: Hospitality-system impact — consider guest services, PMS/POS, and property operations.

CISA has added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

  • CVE-2026-114713 UnrealIRCd Improper Neutralization of Delimiters Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-123039 Check Point Multiple Products Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource Vulnerability

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise.

item.title: 🔴 CISA Adds Six Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
item.description:
Why this matters: Authentication bypass — review access controls and look for unauthorized access.

CISA has added six new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

  • CVE-2026-20320 Cisco BroadWorks Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-111560 Barracuda Networks Multiple Products OS Command Injection Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-111793 Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder Incorrect Resource Transfer Between Spheres Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-116606 Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG) Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-124194 Microsoft Office Outlook Missing User Interaction for Potentially Unsafe Action Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-125350 Google Chromium Use-After-Free Vulnerability 

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors…
